newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu aide urges further Hapoalim asset sales.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu aide urges further Hapoalim asset sales.

text.p: Moshe Leon, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's economic adviser, said on Thursday he is preparing a plan to force Bank Hapoalim to sell its remaining non-bank holdings and its small-bank subsidiaries.
His proposal comes as the government is seeking to sell a controlling stake in Hapoalim, Israel's largest banking group.
"I don't think it's going to affect the sale of the bank," Leon said. "Preventing concentration in the economy is more important than privatisation."
Treasury officials said they had not been told about the plan, and Bank of Israel officials warned that forcing further changes on the banking group would hinder its sale.

Last year the government approved legislation forcing the banks to reduce their holdings in non-bank companies initially to a ceiling of 25 percent of equity. Hapoalim is also required to sell its full holding in either Koor Industries or Clal Israel.
Leon said his plan called for Hapoalim to fully divest itself of both Koor and Clal. He said the proposal that Hapoalim also sell off its small-bank subsidiaries was still under consideration.
